column4: Visit note | 2026-01-19 11:00 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Tamim Gazi, 76, male. Mr. Gazi attends for a follow-up review regarding his blood pressure. He reports experiencing frequent headaches upon waking, occasional dizziness during daily chores, and mentioned that he first noted an elevated reading on a pharmacy machine while buying other medicines in Kushtia. He is retired and works around the home as a homemaker, supporting his family. He has a known history of Bronchial asthma, which remains stable without recent exacerbations. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or visual blurring. On clinical examination, his blood pressure is recorded at BP 156/107 mmHg, pulse is 86 bpm and regular, and his weight is 66 kg. Cardiovascular examination reveals normal heart sounds with no added murmurs, and his chest is clear to auscultation bilaterally. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: chronic follow-up; continue current medicines, no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. He was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk for 30 minutes daily, and check his blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2026-01-26 10:30 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Kawsar Matubbar, 79, male. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

He denies dysphagia, vomiting blood, or unintended weight loss. On examination, his BMI is 27.8, BP is 111/86 mmHg, pulse is 79 bpm, and weight is 79 kg. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests unless symptoms persist; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today.
